name: OK-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong R partisan lean (R+17 PVI) in a safe Oklahoma seat
Longtime incumbent Tom Cole with $2.6M cash on hand vs. $19.5K for the Democrat
Prediction markets price Cole at ~97% to win
No public polling; fundamentals dominate the forecast
model.rationale: Cole is a well-funded incumbent in a district leaning Republican by 17 points, and the Democrat has raised only about $115K with minimal cash on hand. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Cole win, so the forecast stays at the baseline margin.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Cole health issue could tighten the race, but nothing in the evidence suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, and Tom Cole has held it for years with little general-election difficulty. He enters the race with a large financial advantage, roughly $2.6 million on hand, while Democrat Mitchell Jacob has raised about $115,000 and has under $20,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Cole, and no public polls of the race are available.

With no polling and no expert ratings, the outlook rests on the district's strong Republican lean, Cole's incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets give Cole about a 97% chance of winning. The forecast calls this race Safe Republican, with Cole expected to win by a wide margin.
